chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who marries a woman and also marries the mother of her child (from another man), and he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with that.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (from a different father)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry a woman and her mother at the same time in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific nuance in Islamic marriage law, distinguishing between the general prohibition of marrying two sisters simultaneously and the permissibility of marrying a woman and her half-sister (sharing one parent). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms that since the mother is the child of a different father, she is not considered a full sister to the first wife, thereby removing the impediment of 'sisterhood' (ukhtayn) that would otherwise forbid concurrent marriage. This ruling highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence in interpreting the Quranic verse on prohibited kinship, emphasizing that the prohibition applies to full and half-sisters on the maternal side, but the paternal half-sister is permissible to marry concurrently with her sister.
